# Sigma-algebra generated by a random variable

↑ **Parent:** [Sigma-algebra](sigma-algebra.md)

For a real [random variable](random-variable-split.md) $X$ on a [probability space](probability-space-split.md), $\sigma(X)$ is the smallest [sigma-algebra](sigma-algebra.md) making $X$ a [measurable function](measurable-function.md) into the [Borel sigma-algebra](borel-sigma-algebra.md) on $\mathbb R$. The collection of all [inverse images](preimage.md) of [Borel sets](borel-set.md) is already a [sigma-algebra](sigma-algebra.md), since [inverse images](preimage.md) preserve [complements](complement-of-a-set.md) and [countable unions](countable-union.md); this proves the displayed formula without completing any [measure](measure-split.md).
